# A conserving completion of P14 during nucleosynthesis

**For the reference coupling, making P14 conserve energy leaves its abundance tension essentially unchanged.** The scalar peaks at 2.12e-05 of the radiation density near 0.197 MeV. Slower expansion lets more neutrons decay and burns more deuterium. With the published Planck baryon density and Gaussian-process rates, standard expansion is 15.5 times as likely as the physical model, compared with 16.5 for the two-epoch clock proxy. This diagnostic uses the registered mass history. Its field energy and abundance likelihood depend on the chosen completion.

## Action and reconstruction

Use a flat FLRW solution of the Einstein-frame action, with reduced Planck mass M and all material species (including cold dark matter) coupled to the atomic metric.

$$S=\int d^4x\sqrt{-g}\left[\frac{M^2}{2}R-\frac12(\nabla\phi)^2-V(\phi)\right]+S_m[\psi,A^2(\phi)g_{\mu\nu}].$$

Write N = ln a_E, N_t = −ln(1+z_t), with z_t = 10. The registration fixes q = 0.000865, ln A = q min(N−N_t, 0), and a_atomic = A a_E. Choose the early coupling magnitude β = 1 and the monotonic trajectory φ/M = k(N−N_t), k = |q|/β. Then ln A(φ) = sign(q) β min(φ/M, 0). A is constant on the late branch while the field continues to roll. The q = 0 limit is a constant field and vacuum density.

Let B and p be the Einstein-frame material density and pressure, Θ = B−3p, U = φ̇²/2+V and α = d ln A/dφ. Dots use Einstein proper time and primes below use N.

$$3M^2H_E^2=B+U,\qquad \ddot\phi+3H_E\dot\phi+V_{,\phi}=-\alpha\Theta,\qquad B'+3(B+p)=s\Theta,\qquad s=(\ln A)'.$$

$$U'+k^2 U=-k^2 B-s\Theta,\qquad K=\frac{k^2}{6}(B+U),\qquad V(\phi)=U(N)-K(N),\qquad N=N_t+\phi/(kM).$$

These formulas specify a single-valued potential by quadrature. Use the integrating factor exp(k²N) and set U(today) by flatness with h = 0.6727 and ω_m = 0.14257. The trajectory, coupling strength and present vacuum density are choices. Once they are set, the field equation fixes the potential along the trajectory. The exact kink in A and V gives finite one-sided forces. U, φ̇ and H_E are continuous across it. Atomic H has the registered one-sided clock-rate step.

With P_tot = p+K−V, the exchange terms cancel in (B+U)′ = −3(B+U+P_tot). The numerical check differences the endpoint total densities and independently integrates the total enthalpy over each cell. The maximum absolute discrepancy divided by the integrated enthalpy term is 1.11e-08 from today through BBN and 7.25e-12 in the cells touching the transition.

## Expansion at fixed atomic temperature

Electromagnetic entropy conservation gives a_atomic = (T₀/T)[2/g_s(T)]^(1/3) with T₀ = 2.7255 K. Integrating the equilibrium electron–positron phase space supplies both g_s and the pair trace. Free-streaming neutrinos have Tν/T = (g_s/5.5)^(1/3), with N_eff = 3.044 in their energy density. B and Θ are A⁴ times their atomic values. Dust and the pairs source the field. Photons and massless neutrinos have zero trace. Atomic clocks measure H_atomic = (1+s)H_E/A. Both proxies in the table are squared expansion rates.

## Network validation

At ω_b = 0.02237, the late baryon/photon ratio is 6.12446e-10. Before annihilation the code multiplies this by g_s/2. The weak rates integrate E p Eν² dE with Fermi occupation and final-state blocking for beta decay, lepton captures and their inverses. Both the thermal and vacuum integrals include the leading electron–proton Coulomb factor. Pure Born rates give Yₚ = 0.24294, outside the helium validation tolerance. The vacuum integral sets the normalization to τ_n = 878.4 s. The neglect of recoil and the remaining radiative corrections limits the absolute helium accuracy. [Weak rates and normalization, Pitrou et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.08023)

The nuclear network evolves n, p, D, ³H, ³He and ⁴He by an implicit second-order backward difference in −ln T. Reverse nuclear rates use detailed balance with nuclear masses, spin weights and identical-pair factors. It starts in weak equilibrium at 10 MeV and follows residual burning to 0.001 MeV. Nuclear reactions start above the deuterium bottleneck, after the high-temperature weak-only phase.

## What the registration leaves free

For traceless radiation, the early particular solution gives U/B = k²/(4−k²). A specified mass drift fixes the product of coupling and field velocity. It leaves their individual values free. The pairs give a further contribution near annihilation. As an illustration, choose β by requiring the pure-radiation expression to cancel the clock and mass suppression at 0.1 MeV. With β = 0.00258 the same registered mass history has U/ρ_rad = 0.0293 there. The integrated H ratio is 1.00016, and the helium and deuterium ratios become 0.99932 and 1.00079. This choice illustrates degeneracy and has no independent calibration.

## Limits

A full CMB spectrum fit with perturbations would determine the baryon density and its uncertainty for a model with a 0.79% decrease of G in atomic units at recombination. The published and widened treatments show the dependence on that missing information. The network transfers fractional changes computed at one baryon density to each published prediction. It omits heavier nuclides, finite-temperature QED, neutrino transport and nuclear-rate uncertainty propagation. The uncertainties in the likelihood come from the published analyses.

The exact freeze is an imposed kink. This construction establishes a homogeneous solution. Its initial-condition stability, structure formation and scalar-mediated forces require separate tests. A² measures the tensor coupling in atomic units. On scales shorter than the scalar range, unscreened scalar exchange multiplies the Newtonian force by 1+2β² = 3 on the early branch. These abundance data test the cosmological expansion. They do not score the registration.
